problem: The trap says it is wrong to use H = Iω when I is taken about a point that is 'not on the rotation axis or not G'. That contradicts Section 1, which correctly teaches H_O = I_O ω for a fixed axis through O, where O is on the axis but is usually not G. A student will read the trap and think the valid I_O formula is a mistake.
fix: Using H = Iω with I taken about a point that is neither the mass centre G nor a point on the fixed rotation axis. In fixed-axis rotation, I about any point on the axis (not only G) is allowed; in general plane motion, H about a point off the axis also needs the r × m v_G term.

problem: The note gives a bare number 'H₂ − H₁ = −100' with no unit, while every other number in the chapter carries a unit.
fix: Write 'H₂ − H₁ = −100 kg·m²/s' (the same as N·m·s) to match the impulse node.
